canonical_topic: Replicating portfolios as the basis of option pricing
definition: Modern option theory prices an option by constructing a portfolio of the underlying (and other assets) that replicates the option's payoff, rather than by directly forecasting future prices.
core_idea: This shift reduced the need to predict future prices accurately, which matters especially for option sellers, who must be willing to quote whatever product a buyer wants and cannot selectively predict only the assets they prefer.
key_points: Option pricing has two steps: (1) model the statistical distribution of likely underlying price movements, then (2) determine how to replicate the option's payoff under those probabilities.
Replication reduces reliance on directional price forecasting.
Option sellers benefit particularly, since they must quote prices on whatever a buyer wants to trade and cannot pick only assets they're confident forecasting.
relationships: Connects to delta/hedge ratio and arbitrage-free pricing
trading_implications: An option seller can price and hedge a position via replication without needing an accurate directional price forecast.
